sentences.text: Isurolamna was a member of the family Lamnidae, which falls within the class Chondrichthyes, the group containing cartilaginous fish like sharks and rays.
The genus is defined by a small elliptical hole on the tongue side of the tooth root, triangular cusps on most teeth, and a thick root with nearly vertical margins.
Isurolamna inflata stands out as the earliest and most gracile species within the genus.
In contrast, Isurolamna gracilis represents the most robust species known from the genus.
This animal first appeared in the Selandian age of the Paleocene and went extinct by the end of the Rupelian age of the Oligocene, spanning a time range from 66 to 15.98 million years ago.
Isurolamna inflata lived in North Africa, Europe, and North America during the Late Palaeocene and Early Eocene.
Isurolamna bajarunasi is a robust species found mainly in Kazakhstan during the Mid-Late Eocene.
Isurolamna vandenbroeki is a rare species from the Early Oligocene found in Northwestern Europe and Kazakhstan.
Isurolamna schoutedeni lived during the Late Early Ypresian stage of the Eocene epochs.
There is debate regarding whether Isurolamna vandenbroeki should be kept in its own genus or placed within Isurolamna, though many authors follow the diagnosis placing it in Isurolamna.
